examples.en: I was overwhelmed by the atmosphere when I saw the huge stage.

examples.ko: 관객들은 그 가수의 목소리에 압도돼서 아무 말도 못 했어요.
examples.en: The audience was overwhelmed by the singer's voice and couldn't say a word.

examples.ko: 높은 산 앞에 서면 크기에 압도되는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people are overwhelmed by the size when they stand in front of a tall mountain.

examples.ko: 상대 팀의 기세에 압도되면 경기를 망칠 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you get overwhelmed by the other team's momentum, you can ruin the game.
I was worried I would be overwhelmed in the interview room.

examples.ko: 그 영화의 화면에 압도된 채로 한참 앉아 있었어요.
examples.en: I sat there for a long time, overwhelmed by the visuals of that movie.

explain: '압도되다'는 누군가의 힘이나 분위기에 눌려서 기가 죽는 느낌을 말해요. 보통 '~에 압도되다'로 쓰고, 무대, 기세, 크기처럼 큰 것 앞에서 자주 써요. 내가 상대를 누르는 쪽이면 '압도하다'를 써요.
explain_en: 압도되다 describes feeling pressed down by someone's power or by the atmosphere. It is usually used as '~에 압도되다' in front of something big, like a stage, momentum, or sheer size. When you are the one overpowering the other side, use 압도하다.

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 경기 내내 상대를 압도했어요.
examples.en: Our team dominated the opponent throughout the game.

examples.ko: 그 배우의 연기는 다른 사람들을 압도해요.
examples.en: That actor's performance overpowers everyone else.

examples.ko: 큰 소리로 상대를 압도하려고 하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't try to overpower the other person by shouting.

examples.ko: 이번 시험에서 그 학생은 모두를 압도하는 점수를 받았어요.
examples.en: In this exam, that student got a score that outshone everyone.

examples.ko: 화려한 색깔이 보는 사람을 압도하고 있어요.
examples.en: The brilliant colors overwhelm the viewer.

examples.ko: 저 선수는 힘으로 압도하기보다 기술로 이겨요.
examples.en: That player wins with skill rather than overpowering with strength.

explain: '압도하다'는 실력, 힘, 분위기로 상대를 훨씬 앞서거나 눌러 버릴 때 써요. 스포츠 뉴스에서 '경기를 압도하다'가 자주 나와요. 같은 일을 당하는 쪽에서 말하면 '압도되다'가 돼요.
explain_en: 압도하다 is used when you are far ahead of or overpower the other side in skill, strength, or atmosphere. In sports news, '경기를 압도하다' appears often. From the side that gets overpowered, the verb becomes 압도되다.

en: commemorate; pay tribute to the dead

examples.en: People gathered to commemorate the victims.

examples.ko: 우리는 돌아가신 할아버지를 추모하며 꽃을 놓았어요.
examples.en: We laid flowers in memory of our late grandfather.

examples.ko: 오늘은 전쟁에서 목숨을 잃은 분들을 추모하는 날이에요.
examples.en: Today is a day to remember those who lost their lives in the war.

examples.ko: 친구들이 그를 추모하려고 작은 음악회를 열었어요.
examples.en: His friends held a small concert to honor his memory.

examples.ko: 학교에서 일 분 동안 조용히 추모해요.
examples.en: At school, we quietly observe a minute of remembrance.

examples.ko: 많은 사람이 그 가수를 추모해서 노래를 다시 들었어요.
examples.en: Many people honored that singer by listening to his songs again.

explain: '추모하다'는 세상을 떠난 사람을 기억하고 기리는 행동에 써요. 슬퍼하는 마음을 말하는 '애도하다'보다 모여서 꽃을 놓거나 행사를 하는 느낌이 강해요. '추모식', '추모 공간'처럼 명사로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: 추모하다 is for remembering and honoring someone who has passed away. Compared with 애도하다, which is about the feeling of grief, 추모하다 sounds more like an action, such as laying flowers or holding a ceremony. It also appears as a noun in words like 추모식 (memorial service).

examples.en: Our team narrowly lost in the final.

examples.ko: 그는 한 번도 패배한 적이 없는 선수예요.
examples.en: He is a player who has never been defeated.

examples.ko: 패배해도 다음 경기에서 다시 하면 돼요.
examples.en: Even if you lose, you can try again in the next game.

examples.ko: 저는 패배할 때마다 더 열심히 연습해요.
examples.en: Every time I lose, I practice harder.

examples.ko: 약한 팀한테 패배하다니 믿을 수가 없어요.
examples.en: I can't believe they lost to a weak team.

examples.ko: 어제 게임에서 동생에게 패배해서 기분이 안 좋아요.
examples.en: I lost to my younger sibling in the game yesterday, so I'm in a bad mood.

explain: 일상에서는 '지다'를 더 많이 써요. '패배하다'는 뉴스, 스포츠 기사, 글에서 자주 나오는 딱딱한 말이에요. 반대말은 '이기다'와 '승리하다'예요.
explain_en: In daily talk Koreans say 지다 more often. 패배하다 is the stiffer word you see in news, sports reports, and writing. The opposites are 이기다 and 승리하다.

examples.en: The old bridge suddenly collapsed.
The building almost collapsed in the earthquake.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 오면 산이 붕괴되는 일이 있어요.
examples.en: When it rains a lot, hillsides sometimes collapse.

examples.ko: 가족이 아프자 우리 집 생활이 붕괴돼 버렸어요.
examples.en: When a family member got sick, our household life fell apart.
They rescued people from inside the collapsed building.
Once trust crumbles, it is hard to rebuild.

explain: '무너지다'가 일상에서 쓰는 말이고, '붕괴되다'는 뉴스나 글에서 건물, 다리, 제도, 관계가 크게 무너질 때 써요. 이미 '되다'가 붙은 말이라 '붕괴되어지다'처럼 겹쳐 쓰지 않아요. 누가 일부러 무너뜨릴 때는 '무너뜨리다'를 써요.
explain_en: 무너지다 is the everyday word. 붕괴되다 is for news and writing, when buildings, bridges, systems, or relationships collapse on a large scale. It already has the passive 되다, so don't double it as 붕괴되어지다. When someone brings something down on purpose, use 무너뜨리다.

examples.en: Height is passed from parents to children.

examples.ko: 이 병은 가족에게 유전될 수 있어요.
examples.en: This disease can be inherited within a family.
I learned how eye color is inherited.
My grandmother's curly hair was passed down to me too.
The inherited trait showed up in the child just as it was.
There are also many illnesses that are not inherited.

explain: '유전되다'는 키, 병, 머리카락처럼 부모에게서 몸의 특징이 전해지는 것을 과학적으로 말할 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '엄마를 닮았어요'처럼 '닮다'를 훨씬 많이 써요. '유전자', '유전병'도 함께 알아 두세요.
explain_en: 유전되다 is the scientific way to say that body traits like height, illness, or hair type pass from parents to children. In everyday talk, Koreans say '엄마를 닮았어요' with 닮다 far more often. Related words to learn are 유전자 (gene) and 유전병 (hereditary disease).

examples.en: That puppy was adopted by a good family.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 입양된 친구가 친부모님을 찾았어요.
examples.en: A friend who was adopted as a child found their birth parents.

examples.ko: 유기견들이 새 집에 입양되면 행복해 보여요.
examples.en: Abandoned dogs look happy when they are adopted into a new home.
The baby was adopted and went to a faraway country.

examples.ko: 그 고양이는 입양되기 전에는 보호소에서 지냈어요.
examples.en: That cat stayed at a shelter before it was adopted.

examples.ko: 다음 주에 이 고양이도 입양될 거예요.
examples.en: This cat will be adopted next week too.

explain: '입양되다'는 아이나 동물이 새 가족에게 가는 쪽에서 말해요. 가족이 되어 주는 쪽에서 말하면 '입양하다'예요. 반려동물을 데려올 때도 '입양'을 많이 써서, 동물을 '사다'라고 하지 않고 '입양하다'라고 하는 사람이 많아요.
explain_en: 입양되다 is said from the side of the child or animal that goes to a new family. From the side of the one taking them in, use 입양하다. Koreans also say 입양 for bringing home a pet, and many people prefer 입양하다 over 사다 for animals.

examples.en: My spouse and I decided to adopt a child.
I adopted a stray dog last month.
You have to think carefully when you adopt.
My friend adopted a cat from a shelter and is raising it.
The whole family loves the child they adopted.
If you want to adopt a pet, prepare your home first.

explain: '입양하다'는 아이를 법적으로 자녀로 받아들일 때뿐 아니라 보호소의 동물을 데려와 키울 때도 써요. 펫숍이나 브리더에게서 돈을 내고 데려오는 것은 '분양받다'라고 하고, 보호소에서 데려오면 '입양하다'가 자연스러워요. 새 가족에게 가는 쪽은 '입양되다'예요.
explain_en: 입양하다 is used for legally taking a child as your own, and also for bringing home an animal from a shelter. Getting an animal from a pet shop or breeder by paying is called 분양받다, while taking one from a shelter is naturally 입양하다. From the side of the one who goes to the new family, it is 입양되다.

examples.en: This match was ruled a draw.

examples.ko: 검사 결과 아무 문제가 없다고 판정돼요.
examples.en: The test result is judged to show no problem.

examples.ko: 그 공이 아웃으로 판정되면 점수가 안 나요.
examples.en: If that ball is ruled out, no point is scored.

examples.ko: 심사 끝에 이 그림은 일등으로 판정되었어요.
examples.en: After the judging, this painting was ruled first place.

examples.ko: 불량으로 판정된 제품은 팔 수 없어요.
examples.en: Products judged to be defective cannot be sold.
I'm curious how the result will be decided.

explain: '판정되다'는 심판, 심사위원, 의사가 내린 결정으로 결과가 정해질 때 써요. 주어는 사람이 아니라 경기, 공, 제품, 검사 결과예요. 결정을 내리는 쪽은 '판정하다'이고, '판정을 내리다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: 판정되다 is used when a referee, a judging panel, or a doctor's decision settles a result. The subject is not a person but things like a match, a ball, a product, or test results. The one making the decision uses 판정하다, or the phrase '판정을 내리다'.

examples.en: The umpire ruled that ball out.

examples.ko: 의사가 검사 결과를 보고 병이 아니라고 판정해요.
examples.en: The doctor looks at the test results and rules that it is not an illness.

examples.ko: 심사위원들은 점수를 보고 우승자를 판정할 거예요.
examples.en: The judges will decide the winner by looking at the scores.
It is hard to rule on which side won.

examples.ko: 판정하는 사람은 한쪽 편을 들면 안 돼요.
examples.en: The person who makes the ruling must not take a side.

examples.ko: 사진을 보고 진짜인지 판정해서 알려 주세요.
examples.en: Look at the photo, decide whether it's real, and let me know.

explain: '판정하다'는 정해진 기준을 보고 맞는지, 이겼는지, 문제가 있는지 결정을 내릴 때 써요. 심판, 심사위원, 의사가 주어로 많이 나와요. 복싱에서 점수로 이기면 '판정승', 지면 '판정패'라고 해요.
explain_en: 판정하다 is used when someone applies set criteria to decide whether something is correct, who won, or whether there is a problem. Referees, judges, and doctors are common subjects. In boxing, winning on points is called 판정승 and losing on points is 판정패.

examples.en: That movie was really romantic.
A candlelit dinner is romantic.
My boyfriend wrote me a romantic letter.
He is someone who expresses love romantically.
We are not a romantic couple.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날은 로맨틱해서 걷고 싶어요.
examples.en: Rainy days feel romantic, so I want to go for a walk.

explain: '로맨틱하다'는 사랑하는 사이의 분위기, 사람, 장소를 말할 때 써요. 같은 뜻의 '낭만적이다'는 조금 더 글 같고, 사랑이 아니어도 여행이나 꿈처럼 낭만이 있는 것에 써요. 영화 장르 '로맨틱 코미디'는 줄여서 '로코'라고 해요.
explain_en: 로맨틱하다 describes the mood of a loving couple, a person, or a place. The similar 낭만적이다 sounds a bit more literary and also fits non-love things such as travel or dreams. The film genre 'romantic comedy' is shortened to 로코.

en: paralyze; numb; bring to a standstill

examples.ko: 이 약은 신경을 마비시키는 성분이 들어 있어요.
examples.en: This medicine contains an ingredient that numbs the nerves.
The heavy snow brought the city's traffic to a standstill.

examples.ko: 큰 홍수가 마을 전체를 마비시킬 정도였어요.
examples.en: The big flood was enough to bring the whole town to a standstill.

examples.ko: 독이 몸을 마비시켜서 움직일 수 없었어요.
examples.en: The poison paralyzed the body, so I couldn't move.

examples.ko: 두려움이 사람을 마비시켜 버릴 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes fear can paralyze a person.
The union tried to bring the subway to a halt with a strike.

explain: '마비시키다'는 몸의 감각이나 기능, 도시의 기능을 멈추게 할 때 써요. 원인이 되는 쪽이 주어예요. 치과에서 아픔을 없애는 주사는 보통 '마취'라고 해요. 결과를 말하면 '마비되다'를 쓰는데, '교통이 마비되다'가 뉴스에서 더 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 마비시키다 means to stop a body's sensation or function, or a city's functions. The cause is the subject. The shot a dentist gives to take away pain is usually called 마취 (anesthesia). For the result, Koreans use 마비되다, and '교통이 마비되다' (traffic is paralyzed) appears more often in the news.

examples.ko: 큰 사고 앞에서 저는 너무 무력했어요.
examples.en: In the face of the big accident, I was completely powerless.

examples.ko: 아픈 친구를 보면서 아무것도 못 해 무력하게 느꼈어요.
examples.en: Watching my sick friend, I felt helpless because I could do nothing.

examples.ko: 그는 무력한 표정으로 한참을 앉아 있었어요.
examples.en: He sat for a long time with a helpless look.
Since things keep failing, I feel more and more powerless.

examples.ko: 혼자서는 무력하지만 함께하면 달라질 수 있어요.
examples.en: Alone we are powerless, but together things can change.

examples.ko: 너무 무력해서 아무 말도 못 했어요.
examples.en: I felt so helpless that I couldn't say anything.

explain: '무력하다'는 상황 앞에서 내가 할 수 있는 힘이나 방법이 없다는 느낌이에요. 의욕이 없어서 힘이 빠진 '무기력하다'와 달라요. 무력한 것은 힘이 없는 쪽이고, 무기력한 것은 하고 싶은 마음이 없는 쪽이에요.
explain_en: 무력하다 is the feeling that you have no power or way to act in a situation. It differs from 무기력하다, which means lacking the will or energy to do anything. 무력하다 is about having no ability, and 무기력하다 is about having no drive.

examples.en: That drama airs every Saturday.
I watched the program that aired yesterday.

examples.ko: 새 예능이 다음 달부터 방영될 거예요.
examples.en: The new variety show will start airing next month.
This film was not aired in Korea.
That drama became popular as soon as it aired.

examples.ko: 오래전에 방영됐던 만화를 다시 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to watch the cartoon that aired a long time ago again.

explain: '방영되다'는 TV로 드라마, 영화, 만화 같은 영상이 나올 때 써요. 라디오나 뉴스까지 넓게 말할 때는 '방송되다'를 써요. 방송국 쪽이 주어면 '방영하다', 프로그램이 주어면 '방영되다'예요.
explain_en: 방영되다 is used when a video program such as a drama, film, or cartoon is shown on TV. For a broader sense that includes radio and news, Koreans use 방송되다. When the broadcaster is the subject it is 방영하다, and when the program is the subject it is 방영되다.

examples.ko: 그 그룹은 인기가 많았는데 갑자기 해체됐어요.
examples.en: That group was very popular, but it suddenly broke up.
I saw the old building being taken apart.
We each try so that our family doesn't fall apart.
If the company is dissolved, what will happen to the employees?
The members of the band that broke up got back together.
The old machine was taken apart and sold part by part.

explain: '해체되다'는 아이돌 그룹이나 팀처럼 하나로 묶였던 것이 끝나거나, 건물이나 기계가 부품으로 뜯어질 때 써요. 모임이 끝나서 흩어지는 것은 '해산되다'를 많이 써요. 반대말은 '결성되다'예요.
explain_en: 해체되다 is used when something that was held together, such as an idol group or a team, ends, or when a building or machine is taken apart. For a meeting that simply ends and people disperse, 해산되다 is more common. The opposite is 결성되다 (to be formed).

examples.en: The agency decided to disband the group.
The workers took down the old building.
I took the watch apart and examined its parts.
The boss is trying to disband the team.
If you dissolve the company, the employees lose their jobs.

examples.ko: 책상을 해체하는 데 한 시간이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took an hour to take the desk apart.

explain: '해체하다'는 팀이나 그룹을 끝내는 것부터 기계나 구조물을 뜯는 것까지 넓게 써요. 기계나 가구를 부품으로 나눌 때는 '분해하다', 건물을 없앨 때는 '철거하다'가 더 구체적이에요. 모임을 끝내고 흩어지게 할 때는 '해산하다'를 써요.
explain_en: 해체하다 covers a wide range, from ending a team or group to taking apart machines or structures. For splitting a machine or furniture into parts, 분해하다 is more specific, and for tearing down a building, 철거하다. To end a gathering and send people away, use 해산하다.

examples.en: Even when failures kept piling up, I didn't give up.
The same question kept coming up, and I got tired of answering.
As accidents kept happening, people became anxious.
My body is tired because of the repeated overtime.
If this keeps happening, you lose trust.
After repeated efforts, I passed the exam.

explain: '거듭되다'는 같은 일이 연달아 이어지거나 쌓일 때 써요. '반복되다'보다 글 같은 말이고, 실패, 사고, 노력, 논란처럼 계속 겹치는 일에 잘 어울려요. '거듭되는', '거듭된'처럼 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 때 특히 많이 써요.
explain_en: 거듭되다 is used when the same thing keeps happening one after another or piling up. It sounds more literary than 반복되다 and fits things that overlap again and again, such as failures, accidents, efforts, or controversies. It is especially common in the modifier forms 거듭되는 and 거듭된.

examples.ko: 그는 실패를 거듭하면서 많은 것을 배웠어요.
examples.en: He learned a lot while failing again and again.
The two companies held round after round of negotiations.

examples.ko: 거듭해서 사과했지만 친구는 용서해 주지 않았어요.
examples.en: I apologized again and again, but my friend didn't forgive me.
If you keep practicing, your skills improve.
The repeated efforts finally paid off.
After thinking it over and over, I finally decided.

explain: '거듭하다'는 '실패를 거듭하다', '연습을 거듭하다', '고민을 거듭하다'처럼 '명사+을/를 거듭하다' 모양으로 많이 써요. 같은 일을 하고 또 하는 느낌이라 '반복하다'보다 글 같은 말이에요. '거듭'만 부사로 써서 '거듭 부탁하다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: 거듭하다 is mostly used in the pattern 'noun + 을/를 거듭하다', as in 실패를 거듭하다, 연습을 거듭하다, and 고민을 거듭하다. It carries the feeling of doing the same thing again and again, and it sounds more literary than 반복하다. The adverb 거듭 alone also works, as in 거듭 부탁하다.

en: be involved in; have a hand in

examples.en: My parents don't interfere in my affairs.

examples.ko: 그 사건에 관여한 사람들이 조사를 받았어요.
examples.en: The people involved in that case were investigated.
The boss got directly involved in the work and made the decision.
The government is stepping in on prices.

examples.ko: 저는 그 문제에 관여할 수 없어요.
examples.en: I can't get involved in that matter.
I don't know how far I'm allowed to get involved.

explain: '관여하다'는 어떤 일에 관계를 맺고 끼어든다는 느낌이고, 보통 '일에 관여하다'처럼 '에'와 함께 써요. 모임이나 행사에 같이 하는 '참여하다'와 달리, 남의 일이나 결정에 개입한다는 느낌이 있어서 부정문에 자주 나와요. 더 강하게 나서는 '간섭하다'보다는 중립적이에요.
explain_en: 관여하다 means to step into and have a hand in something, and it is usually paired with 에, as in 일에 관여하다. Unlike 참여하다, which means joining a meeting or event, 관여하다 has the sense of getting involved in someone else's matter or decision, so it often appears in negative sentences. It is more neutral than the stronger 간섭하다 (to meddle).

examples.en: This year I'll concentrate on studying English.
This company focuses its efforts on developing new products.
I'm putting my main effort into exercise for my health.
Before the exam, I focused on review.
Which field are you focusing on these days?

examples.ko: 한 가지에만 주력하면 다른 일을 놓칠 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you focus on just one thing, you may miss other things.

explain: '주력하다'는 '~에 주력하다'로 써서 여러 일 중에 가장 큰 힘을 쏟는 곳을 말해요. '집중하다'는 정신을 한곳에 모으는 느낌이고, '주력하다'는 회사, 팀, 계획의 중심 방향을 말할 때 잘 어울려요. '주력 상품', '주력 분야'처럼 명사로도 써요.
explain_en: 주력하다 is used as '~에 주력하다' to name where you pour the most effort among many tasks. 집중하다 is more about gathering your attention on one spot, while 주력하다 fits the main direction of a company, team, or plan. It also works as a noun-modifier in 주력 상품 (flagship product) and 주력 분야 (main field).

examples.en: Cockroaches are really disgusting.

examples.ko: 그 사진은 너무 혐오스러워서 볼 수 없었어요.
examples.en: That photo was so repulsive that I couldn't look at it.
The room was full of a revolting smell.
It's repulsive that you would say something like that.

examples.ko: 시장 뒷골목에 쌓인 쓰레기가 혐오스럽게 느껴졌어요.
examples.en: The garbage piled up in the market back alley felt disgusting.

examples.ko: 저는 곤충이 혐오스럽지 않아서 만져 봤어요.
examples.en: Insects aren't repulsive to me, so I touched one.

explain: '혐오스럽다'는 ㅂ 불규칙 형용사라서 '혐오스러워요', '혐오스러운'으로 바뀌어요. 벌레를 보고 기분이 나쁠 때는 일상에서 '징그럽다'를 더 많이 쓰고, 행동이나 말이 도덕적으로 역겨울 때는 '역겹다'도 써요. '혐오스럽다'는 그보다 딱딱해서 뉴스나 글에 잘 나와요.
explain_en: 혐오스럽다 is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it becomes 혐오스러워요 and 혐오스러운. In everyday talk, Koreans use 징그럽다 more for bugs, and 역겹다 for morally sickening words or actions. 혐오스럽다 is stiffer than these and appears more in news and writing.

examples.en: I detest lying.
He loathed violence.
Don't do things that people detest.

examples.ko: 서로를 혐오하게 되면 같이 살 수 없어요.
examples.en: If you come to loathe each other, you can't live together.
There's no need to go as far as loathing that person.

examples.ko: 어릴 때부터 벌레를 혐오해서 시골이 싫었어요.
examples.en: I have loathed bugs since I was little, so I disliked the countryside.

explain: '혐오하다'는 '싫어하다'보다 훨씬 강한 감정으로, 생리적으로 못 견디거나 도덕적으로 용납할 수 없을 때 써요. 일상에서 싫은 음식이나 사람에게 가볍게 쓰는 말이 아니에요. '혐오 발언', '혐오 표현'처럼 사회 문제를 말할 때도 나와요.
explain_en: 혐오하다 is far stronger than 싫어하다. Use it when something is physically unbearable or morally unacceptable to you, not for casually disliked food or people. It also appears in social-issue terms like 혐오 발언 (hate speech) and 혐오 표현.

examples.en: If you have a wholesome hobby, your stress decreases.
This game is wholesome even for children.
The habit of spending money sensibly is important.
Don't visit sites that aren't wholesome.
They say that if your body is healthy, your mind becomes sound too.

examples.ko: 회사 재정이 건전해서 오래 일하고 싶어요.
examples.en: The company's finances are sound, so I want to work there a long time.

explain: '건강하다'는 몸이나 마음의 상태가 좋을 때 쓰고, '건전하다'는 생각, 취미, 문화, 재정이 바르고 문제가 없을 때 써요. '건전한 생각', '건전 가요'처럼 쓰고, 몸이 튼튼하다는 말은 보통 '건강하다'를 써요. 반대말은 '불건전하다'예요.
explain_en: 건강하다 is for a good state of body or mind, while 건전하다 is for thoughts, hobbies, culture, or finances that are proper and free of problems. It appears in 건전한 생각 (a sound way of thinking) and 건전 가요 (clean pop songs); for a strong body, people usually say 건강하다. The opposite is 불건전하다.
